title.narrative: Strategic Sector Cooperation Phase 1 project in Ghana- Statistics

description.narrative: The overall objective of the SSC project is to improve the statistical system of Ghana and thereby the foundation for evidence-based policy making and democracy – through increased availability of internationally comparable, independent, accurate and timely statistics.

title.narrative: Accuracy and Coverage of Economic Statistics improved
Not applicable as baseline, impact indicators are not defined for current SSC projects.

target.value:
Output D.1 Consumer Price Index transformed from 10 to 16 regions and updated
Output D.1.A indicator: CPI transformed from 10 to 16 regions
Output D.1.B indicator: Exchange of products and size of samples completed
Output D.1.C indicator: CPI quality document prepared for publication

actual.value: D.1.A: Nearly achieved. Work was completed on the rebasing for 10 regions in 2019, Q3. Ghana has added 6 new regions, which calls for extending the computation to cover the 16 regions. This work is nearly complete via a series of Zoom sessions. D.1.B: Partly achieved. The methodology for exchanging products is well understood. The sample size is under discussion. D.1.C: Not achieved.

title.narrative: Use of Administrative Data Sources for Statistical Production Increased
Not applicable as baseline, impact indicators are not defined for current SSC projects.

target.value:
In progress Output A.1.A indicator: Variables, intervals and format needed for population statistics described
Output A.1.B indicator: Binding agreement(s) on regular data delivery are drafted and ready for signature
Output A.1.C indicator: New MDA data is delivered from at least one source
Output A.1.D indicator: Report detailing the findings from comparing census data to BDR/NIA data

actual.value: In progress A.1.A: Partly achieved. GSS has, with support from Statistics Denmark, made significant outreach to various Ministries, Departments, Authorities (MDAs) to map the kind of data collected including in the Birth and Death Registry (BDR) and National Identification Authority (NIA) and the format in which data can be transported to GSS. Work is ongoing with experts supporting the process. A.1.B: Partly achieved. The BDR under the constitution of Ghana are legally mandated to share data with GSS for statistical use. With NIA and other MDAs, the team at GSS is advised to draft a MoU between GSS and the stakeholders to ensure a binding agreement on how regular data is transferred to GSS and format in which GSS will receive it. Concrete work on drafting the MoUs remain. A.1.C: Not achieved. Work has not yet started.
